topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory framing for the lecture series, outlining course objectives, student cohorts, and key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological concepts of cancer development and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the fundamental concept of cancer as a breakdown in genetic regulation, cellular differentiation, and three-dimensional tissue architecture, alongside experimental models used to study these changes.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and histological progression
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the pathological hallmarks of tumor invasion through the basement membrane, routes of metastatic dissemination, and histological progression from localized precursor lesions to invasive malignancy.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature, clinical risks, and mechanisms of mortality
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the conventions used to name tumors and the physical and physiological mechanisms through which both benign and malignant neoplasms cause clinical disease, complications, and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across humans and other animal species
topics.groupedBecause: They compare epidemiological patterns, common organ sites, and mortality rates of tumors across human populations and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Cancer detection, screening methods, and clinical limitations
topics.groupedBecause: They explore clinical strategies and histological criteria for detecting pre-malignant and early-stage tumors across different organ sites, evaluating their effectiveness and practical limitations.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the closing framing for the lecture, summarizing final reminders for practical sessions and upcoming classes.
